title: India’s ₹4,000 Crore Ramayana Is Heading to Comic-Con — and It Wants to Be the Biggest Film on Earth
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari’s two-part epic starring Ranbir Kapoor will debut its trailer at San Diego Comic-Con in July. With Hans Zimmer, Warner Bros., and IMAX on board, this is Bollywood’s most ambitious global play ever.
body:
If you grew up in a diaspora household where Sunday mornings meant Ramanand Sagar's *Ramayana* on loop — the kind of viewing that made parents late for everything except temple — then what **Nitesh Tiwari** is attempting will either thrill you or terrify you. Probably both.

**Ramayana**, India's most expensive film ever made, is heading to **San Diego Comic-Con** this July for its first global trailer reveal. Let that sink in: an Indian mythological epic, sharing a stage with Marvel and DC, pitched at the same audience that lines up overnight for superhero scoops. This isn't Bollywood going global. This is Bollywood demanding a seat at the blockbuster table and bringing ₹4,000 crore worth of receipts.

## The Numbers That Made Producers Nervous

The two-part saga — **Part 1** releasing **Diwali 2026**, **Part 2** a year later — carries a combined budget of roughly **₹4,000 crore** (approximately $470 million), making it comfortably the most expensive Indian film franchise ever produced. For context, *RRR* cost around ₹550 crore. *Ramayana* costs more than seven *RRRs*.

Producer **Namit Malhotra** (Prime Focus, DNEG) reportedly rejected a ₹700 crore OTT deal for both parts — the highest ever offered for an Indian film — because he's holding out for ₹1,000 crore or more. The message is clear: this film was made for the big screen, and it will live or die there.

## A Cast That Reads Like a Fantasy Draft

**Ranbir Kapoor** leads as **Lord Rama**, and in a surprise move, also plays **Parashurama** in a dual role. **Yash** — the *KGF* franchise machine — is **Ravana**. **Sai Pallavi**, arguably India's most compelling screen presence right now, plays **Sita**. **Sunny Deol** is **Hanuman**. **Ravie Dubey** takes on **Laxman**, and **Arun Govil** — yes, the original Ram from 1987 — returns as **King Dasharatha**, a casting choice so poetic it borders on fan fiction made real.

Ranbir has spoken about how becoming a father to daughter **Raha** transformed his understanding of the role. “Fatherhood changed my lens entirely,” he said in a recent interview. “Playing Ram after holding my daughter — you understand dharma differently.”

## Hans Zimmer Meets AR Rahman

Perhaps the most audacious creative decision: the score is a **joint composition by Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman**. Zimmer, the man behind *Inception*, *Interstellar*, and *The Dark Knight*, working alongside Rahman, who gave the world *Jai Ho*. A live musical event tied to the soundtrack is planned for October 2026. The teaser alone — which hit **18 million YouTube views in 24 hours** — gave audiences a taste of what a Zimmer-Rahman fusion sounds like. It sounds enormous.

## Hollywood Infrastructure, Indian Soul

This isn't just an Indian film with a big budget. The infrastructure is genuinely global. **DNEG** (Tiwari's home turf through Malhotra) is handling VFX across both parts, which together run over **six hours** of footage. **Warner Bros.** is managing international distribution. **IMAX** has confirmed a worldwide release. Early reactions from an LA focus group screening were reportedly very positive, and veteran actress **Dipika Chikhlia** — the original Sita from Ramanand Sagar's series — praised the footage as “very grand, very beautiful.”

Part 2 is already 50% shot, signaling that Tiwari isn't slowing down.

## Why Diaspora Audiences Should Care

For NRIs, this is the film to watch — literally. The SDCC trailer launch, Warner Bros. distribution deal, and IMAX worldwide release mean that for the first time, an Indian mythological epic will arrive in American, British, Canadian, and Australian cinemas with the same marketing muscle as a Hollywood tentpole. No hunting for that one AMC showing at 10 PM on a Tuesday. No waiting three weeks after the India release.

The ₹700 crore OTT rejection also means one thing: you won't be streaming this on **JioCinema** opening weekend. If you want to experience *Ramayana* the way it was designed to be experienced — on the largest screen possible, with a Zimmer-Rahman score rattling your chest — you'll need to be in a theatre on Diwali weekend 2026.

Start planning now. Your parents will want to come.

## What's Next

The SDCC trailer reveal in July will be the first real look at finished footage. Expect the marketing machine to accelerate after that, with Warner Bros. likely rolling out territory-specific campaigns. The Hans Zimmer x AR Rahman live concert event in October could become a cultural moment in its own right. And then, Diwali 2026 — the biggest opening weekend Indian cinema has ever attempted.
